skill.name: xlsx
skill.description: Comprehensive spreadsheet creation, editing, analysis, and validation for Excel, CSV, and TSV files, including formulas, formatting, pandas analysis, and LibreOffice recalculation.
skill.summary: Create, edit, analyze, and validate spreadsheet files with formula-focused workflows.
skill.author: davila7

security_audit.summary: Confirmed findings center on recalc.py executing LibreOffice and writing a persistent macro under the user LibreOffice profile. The hardcoded URL and most SKILL.md backtick or reconnaissance hits are documentation false positives; no prompt injection or data exfiltration intent was found.

remediation.suggestion: Use a temporary LibreOffice user profile and remove macro files after recalculation; ask before writing under home configuration.

remediation.issue: External command execution for formula recalculation
remediation.suggestion: Resolve trusted binary paths, validate timeout values, sandbox LibreOffice, and avoid automatic processing of untrusted workbooks.
Add file size and sheet limits, process a copy, and document resource costs before scanning every cell.

content.value_statement: Spreadsheet work often fails when formulas, formats, and cached values diverge. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through structured Excel creation, analysis, editing, and recalculation checks.
actual_capabilities: Create Excel workbooks with sheets, formulas, styles, widths, and basic charts.
Read and analyze Excel, CSV, and TSV data with pandas-oriented workflows.
Edit existing workbooks while preserving formulas and established formatting patterns.
Recalculate formulas through the bundled LibreOffice helper and report spreadsheet error types.
Apply financial modeling conventions for colors, number formats, assumptions, and source notes.
limitations: Formula recalculation requires LibreOffice and the Python packages used by the helper script.
The helper writes a LibreOffice macro into the user profile unless redesigned.
Complex macros, external links, and proprietary Excel features may not recalculate exactly like Microsoft Excel.
Large workbooks can consume significant CPU and memory because validation scans every cell.

use_cases.title: Build Financial Models
use_cases.description: Create projection workbooks with assumptions, formulas, formatting, and source notes for review.

use_cases.title: Clean Operational Reports
use_cases.description: Read messy spreadsheet exports, summarize key fields, and produce a structured workbook.

use_cases.title: Validate Existing Templates
use_cases.description: Update a workbook while preserving layout, then check formulas for common Excel errors.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Simple Workbook
prompt_templates.prompt: Create an Excel workbook for monthly sales. Include raw data, summary metrics, and formulas for totals and averages.

prompt_templates.title: Analyze Exported Data
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze this CSV export and create an Excel summary workbook with trends, outliers, and clear number formatting.

prompt_templates.title: Update a Template
prompt_templates.prompt: Update this workbook with the new assumptions. Preserve existing formulas, formatting, sheet names, and source notes.

prompt_templates.title: Build and Validate a Model
prompt_templates.prompt: Build a three-statement financial model with linked assumptions, scenario cases, formula checks, and a recalculation review.

output_examples.input: Create a revenue forecast workbook for four quarters.
output_examples.output: A formatted workbook with assumptions, formulas, scenario columns, and a recalculation check summary showing no formula errors.

output_examples.input: Analyze a CSV export of support tickets.
output: A workbook with cleaned ticket data and summary tabs.
Charts for volume, resolution time, and category trends.
Notes explaining data quality issues and recommended fixes.

output_examples.input: Update an existing budget template with new department data.
output_examples.output: The template layout is preserved, requested cells are updated, assumptions are documented, and formula errors are reported for review.

best_practices: Work on a copy before editing templates or running recalculation.
Keep assumptions in separate cells and reference them from formulas.
Run formula recalculation after edits and review every reported error.
anti_patterns: Hardcoding calculated outputs instead of using spreadsheet formulas.
Saving a workbook opened with calculated values only, which can replace formulas.
Running recalculation on untrusted or very large workbooks without review.

faq.question: What file types can this skill work with?
faq.answer: It is designed for Excel files and common tabular formats such as CSV and TSV.

faq.question: Does it preserve existing formulas?
faq.answer: Yes, the guidance emphasizes preserving formulas and formatting when editing existing workbooks.

faq.question: Can it recalculate formulas?
faq.answer: Yes, it includes a LibreOffice-based helper for recalculation when LibreOffice is available.

faq.question: Is it suitable for financial models?
faq.answer: Yes, it includes conventions for assumptions, formulas, colors, number formats, and source documentation.

faq.question: Can it replace Microsoft Excel?
faq.answer: No. Some Excel-specific features, macros, and external links may behave differently in LibreOffice.

faq.question: What security review result matters most?
faq.answer: The main risk is the helper script, which runs LibreOffice and writes a macro into the user profile.
